addedByMain: // Who may be shown as a line's author (#909). A handle is a claim the payload makes, so it is shown only
// when it can be traced here: the transport sender itself, a remote seat this room holds, or its inviter.
// Anything else is shown as the sender (a Bot), marked unverified. A non-handle id is a person or a Bot of
// the other home (#873): this side never resolves those, so the claim stands as it did before.
if (!claim) return sender ? { authorId: sender, authorKind: 'bot' } : { authorId: undefined, authorKind: 'human' }
if (!claim.startsWith('@')) return { authorId: claim, authorKind: kind }
|| currentParticipants(room).some(p => p.remote === true && (p.handle === claim || p.id === claim))
return traced ? { authorId: claim, authorKind: kind } : { authorId: sender || claim, authorKind: 'bot', unverified: true }
// The transport names the Bot that delivered this, and that is the only identity this side can check:
// the envelope's inviter fields are display (#873 keeps its "Shared room from Alice"), never the gate
// that decides which room a share may touch (#909).
// Matched by the transport only (#909): a share that names a room of mine while arriving from a home
// that room does not belong to is refused, not merged in through a fallback lookup.
if (claimed) return { handled: true, refused: 'not-inviter', room: claimed }
// Only a join projects a room here. A line for a remote room nobody shared with this home used to
// create one, named from its own payload (#909).
// The name is display and follows the envelope (#873); the identity follows the transport, so this
// path can never rewrite whose room it is (#909).
// The author claim follows the same rule (#909): a handle this room cannot trace — to the transport
// sender, to one of its own remote seats, or to its inviter — is shown as the Bot that carried the
// envelope, never as that handle. The line itself is kept: a forged claim must not silence a message.

// may touch, which room gets created, or who wrote a line. The transport names the Bot that delivered it,
// and that is the only identity this side can check.
test('#909: a join from another home cannot rewrite or enter a mirror room it does not own', async (t) => {
// Same remote room id, claiming to be the room's inviter, delivered by a home that is not it.

- A local group's **Members · N** card (`group-settings.js`) ends with the plugin rows of slot `flybot.room.members` (`FlyBotRoomMembers` in `flybot-slots.js`), after the note on who leads the group (#892) and on the card's own row padding (`.bt-flybot-room-members`), never in a face or shared (`inbound-share`) room; the rows get `host`, the core endpoint call (also `__flybot__.host`), for `room-invite` / `room-invite-mint` / `room-invite-revoke` (#876, the social plugin's **Invite by link**). Covered by `core/test/room-members-slot.test.js`. Plugin copy that core's dictionary carries is translated through `__flybot__.t` (#892: Invite by link, the Join-or-create dialog), so a zh UI reads it in Chinese. A room a link opened is titled by its own name on the joining home (`roomTitle` in `remote-label.js`: sidebar, header, drawer, brand); "Shared room from …" stays as the sidebar row's hover and the **Shared** tag's title (#892).

addedByMain: - Bot Social conversations are 1:1; it does not list a FlyBot group. When a room gains a granted remote Bot (create-room, addParticipants, or 新建群聊 picking a friend's chat), the host fans out a `FLYBOT-ROOM-SHARE` envelope (`src/shared/room-share.js`) through `flybotSend` (`via: 'room-share'` for join/leave, `via: 'room'` for lines, `meta.roomId` set) so the Bot's owner's FlyBot can project it immediately — including a room with no chat lines yet. Receive is `rt.applyInboundRoomShare` (`origin: 'inbound-share'`, `recordInboundSharedRoom`), labelled **Shared room from \<inviter\>** with the room name stored. The envelope names the person who invited the Bot (#848): a human participant in the room when there is one, else the owner-level `ownerName` / `home` the social plugin keeps on that Bot's member record (read from `whoami`), so a group made from the sidebar no longer says `a friend`; a human participant whose name is this home's own label `You` (an owner with no name yet) is skipped for that owner-level name, so the far side never reads itself as the inviter (#883); a room projected in from an inbound share forwards its own `sharedFrom` inviter instead of this home's owner, so re-sharing never renames the person who invited it. A leave envelope, hide, or grant revoke marks it left/hidden. A projection is **named** from the envelope and **matched** by the transport (#873, #909): `applyInboundRoomShare` still shows `data.inviterName` (so a room carried here by a Chief's Bot reads after the person who invited it), but which room a share may touch is decided by `event.fromHome` / `event.fromHandle` — a share naming a room of mine while arriving from a home that room does not belong to is refused `not-inviter`, and the recorded `sharedFrom` identity only ever follows the transport, so an envelope can be displayed but never re-write whose room it is. Only `op: 'join` projects a room: a `line` envelope for an unknown remote room is refused `unknown-room` instead of opening one named by its own payload. A line keeps its own `who`, or the sender when it names nobody, never the inviter; its `authorId` follows the payload only when the handle traces to the transport sender, a remote seat of that room, or its inviter — otherwise the line is shown as the Bot that delivered it with `unverified: true`, and it is still kept so a forged claim cannot silence a message. `reach()` allows a local member to message a remote that already sits in that room when `roomId` is on the send. Still not team mode.

- **A part is committed before its handoff runs** (`parts.js` `moveOn`): the Bot's `sessionId` / `room.sessions`, the new segment and the `rescued` mark are saved first, so the turn the handoff starts can never see an uncommitted part — a failure handler that did would start a second switch against it and lose the previous part's note, and the rescue would not know it may only happen once. The handoff package is written next; if that fails, the pointer is rolled back (best effort saved, the fresh Session archived, the rescued mark dropped), so the old part is current and the finalizer hands the input on there. Two windows stay open, and both are written down rather than discovered later: a crash after that save and before the handoff package is flushed leaves the fresh part current with no package — the stopped turn's input still goes to it, so no work is lost, but the note is, and the rollback never runs; and the rollback's own save is best effort (`rt.save().catch(() => {})`), so a failing rollback leaves the file showing the fresh part while memory holds the old one, and the next start behaves like the first window. Neither is a reason to clear the pointer before the save: a note lost this way is a part without a handoff note, while clearing first loses the handoff package itself. The move is marked done only after the stopped turn's input and the old inbox messages are forwarded; a switch that never starts (no place, another switch, a read-only host) lets the step continue instead of rejecting its messages, which DSH has already taken out of the inbox. An armed scheduled task keeps the earlier Session active and DSH refuses to archive it, so the switch keeps the `moveSchedules` promise and waits for the move before archiving the earlier part; when the move failed and the refusal reports `schedule` as the only activity, the plain archive is retried with `{ stopActivity: true }` (the way a deletion does, `roster.js:450`), so a finished part is never left active with a task nobody sees; a refusal caused by a job, turn or subagent is not retried, because `stopActivity` would stop that too (#896). Covered by `core/test/work-dir.test.js`, `core/test/part-archive.test.js` and `core/test/bot-messages.test.js`.
